psych-clin-01-c1.text: Jerome Wakefield; entry by Dominic Murphy (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy) (2020). Concepts of Health and Disease. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
psych-clin-01-c1.quote: in Wakefield's version we first judge that a psychological mechanism is not performing the function
psych-clin-01-c1.claim: Jerome Wakefield's influential harmful dysfunction account combines a value component (harm) with a factual component (a mental mechanism failing to perform its evolved function).

psych-clin-01-c2.text: G. L. Engel (1977). The need for a new medical model: a challenge for biomedicine. Science.
psych-clin-01-c2.quote: A biopsychosocial model is proposed that provides a blueprint for research
psych-clin-01-c2.claim: In 1977 George Engel put forward the biopsychosocial model, which holds that biology, psychology, and social context interact in any disorder.

psych-clin-01-c2.text: D. Borsboom and A. O. J. Cramer (2013). Network analysis: an integrative approach to the structure of psychopathology. Annual Review of Clinical Psychology, 9, 91-121.
psych-clin-01-c2.quote: In network approaches to psychopathology, disorders result from the causal interplay between symptoms
psych-clin-01-c2.claim: More recently, Borsboom's network approach treats disorders as self-reinforcing networks of symptoms causing each other, rather than as latent diseases causing symptoms.
